item: NNWeightedHuberWrapper.fit mutates PROCESS-GLOBAL RNG state, and RandomForest / cross_val_score hardcode n_jobs=-1.
detail: Under a job queue running two trainings concurrently, np.random.seed from job B silently reseeds the global numpy RNG that job A's sklearn estimators (any without an explicit random_state) are drawing from — results become non-reproducible in a way that only shows up as small metric drift between identical runs. Separately, n_jobs=-1 inside N concurrent workers spawns N x cores threads; the symptom is a machine that thrashes and a job that 'hangs', not an error. torch.cuda.manual_seed (not manual_seed_all) leaves multi-GPU nondeterministic.
ev: models/nn_whuber.py:313-317 — `torch.manual_seed(random_seed)`, `np.random.seed(random_seed)`, `torch.cuda.manual_seed(random_seed)`. models/rf.py:34 and 42 (`n_jobs=-1`); ml/eval.py:161 (`cross_val_score(..., n_jobs=-1)`). Also models/nn_w…
act: Replace the global seeding with a local torch.Generator passed to the DataLoader plus np.random.default_rng(seed) for any numpy draws, before any concurrency exists. Make n_jobs a parameter defaulting to 1 inside workers. Pin the current be…
note: Unchanged at HEAD in every particular. The NN wrapper still reseeds process-global numpy and torch RNG inside fit, torch.cuda.manual_seed is still the single-device call so multi-GPU stays nondeterministic, and both RFWrapper constructions plus cross_val_score still hardcode n_jobs=-1. Under the queue this is contained rather than fixed: turbotab/jobs.py serializes any job declared uses_global_rng and snapshots/restores around it, so neighbours are safe - but the containment is a lock, i.e. it converts a correctness bug into a throughput cost, and it does nothing about n_jobs=-1, which under N workers still spawns N x cores threads and presents as a hung job rather than an error. Fix the seeding with a local torch.Generator plus np.random.default_rng, and make n_jobs a parameter defaulting to 1 inside workers.

If it consults supports_predict_proba it will offer calibration, ROC curves, and decision-curve analysis for regression models — the branches then call predict_proba, get None back (base default, no exception), and render an empty or crashed panel. The metadata LOOKS authoritative because 8 sibling fields on the same dataclass are load-bearing.

item: BCa acceleration is computed from a jackknife that is capped at 200 leave-one-out replicates and then PADDED to length n with the mean of those 200.

item: PlausibilityGate cannot be sklearn-cloned. It mutates its constructor parameters in __init__, violating the sklearn clone identity contract — and reconcile_pipeline_columns clones UNCONDITIONALLY on every training run.
detail: sklearn.base.clone reads get_params(), deep-copies each value, reconstructs the class, then asserts `param_new is param_old` and raises RuntimeError('Cannot clone object ... as the constructor either does not set or modifies parameter lower_bounds'). PlausibilityGate's __init__ builds a NEW array from whatever it is handed, so the identity check always fails. Consequences, all silent: (1) CROSS-VALIDATION IS SILENTLY DISABLED — pages/06:1561 catches it as `st.warning(f'Cross-validation failed for {model_name}: {cv_error}. Skipping CV.')`, a transient banner, while the results table and the manuscript render complete without CV; (2) SEED SENSITIVITY RETURNS ALL NaN — pages/08:211 appends `{'s…
ev: ml/preprocess_operators.py:50-55 `self.lower_bounds = np.array([np.nan if v is None else float(v) for v in lower_bounds], dtype=float)`. Clone sites: ml/pipeline.py:531/534/553 (inside reconcile_pipeline_columns, called at pages/06:1299 eve…
act: Move all coercion out of __init__ into fit(), storing as fitted attributes (self.lower_bounds_, self.upper_bounds_); keep __init__ as bare assignment, exactly as UnitHarmonizer does. Change OutlierCapping to `self.params = params` and defau…
note: Fixed as the row prescribed: PlausibilityGate.__init__ is bare assignment and the coercion moved into fit() onto lower_bounds_/upper_bounds_, exactly as UnitHarmonizer's docstring documents; OutlierCapping stores self.params = params unmodified and resolves the default inside fit(). TWO CORRECTIONS TO THIS ROW'S ACCOUNT, both measured rather than reasoned. (1) THE CONSEQUENCE WAS LOUDER THAN 'CV SILENTLY DISABLED'. reconcile_pipeline_columns runs at pages/06:1209, BEFORE model_pipeline.fit at :1222, inside the per-model try whose handler at :1515 is st.error('Training failed: ...'). So with bounds configured and X_train a DataFrame, no model trained at all and the message read 'Training failed: Cannot clone object PlausibilityGate(lower_bounds=array([...]))' - loud, but naming a constructor identity check rather than plausibility bounds. The silently-skipped-CV symptom is the one that appears when the reconcile checkpoint is bypassed (X_train not a DataFrame). Both are fixed by the same change. (2) THE DEFECT WAS NOT LIMITED TO PLAUSIBILITY BOUNDS. OutlierCapping's self.params = params or {} broke clone specifically for a FALSY params dict, and ml/pipeline.py:229 passes numeric_outlier_params or {} - so the app's own no-parameters outlier configuration was the unclonable one. A project with outlier capping and NO plausibility bounds at all failed exactly the same way, which the row's framing (sibling-of TEST-003, 'whenever plausibility bounds are configured') excludes.
verified_ev: ml/preprocess_operators.py:46-80 (PlausibilityGate), :93-128 (OutlierCapping); ml/pipeline.py:229

item: _lockbox_signature and _content_fingerprint both rest on int(pd.util.hash_pandas_object(df, index=False).sum()), which silently wraps on int64 overflow, varies across pandas versions, and returns None/degrades on unhashable cells.
detail: Two materially different frames can produce the same sum (wraparound is a real collision channel over large frames), so set_data treats a genuine data change as a benign rerun and every stale model, metric and figure survives. Conversely a pandas upgrade changes the hash for identical data, so the first render after a deploy redraws the lockbox and wipes the user's work with a banner that says the data changed.
ev: utils/test_lockbox.py:46 and utils/session_state.py:228 (`except Exception: return None` → set_data falls back to schema-only invalidation, per the docstring at :224-226).
act: Use an explicit, version-pinned digest (e.g. blake2b over the parquet bytes of a canonicalized frame) and store the digest algorithm id in the Project. Never let 'cannot fingerprint' silently mean 'unchanged' — make it mean 'assume changed'…
note: Unchanged at HEAD. Both the lockbox signature and the invalidation fingerprint still rest on a SUM of per-row hashes, which wraps silently on int64 and is therefore a real collision channel over large frames - and set_data treats a collision as a benign rerun, so every stale model, metric and figure survives a genuine data change. The failure runs the other way too: pd.util.hash_pandas_object is not a stability guarantee across pandas versions, so the first render after an upgrade can redraw the lockbox and wipe the user's work under a banner saying the data changed. And the unhashable-cell path degrades to None, which MINE-010 covers. Use a version-pinned digest over canonicalized bytes, store the algorithm id in the Project, and never let 'cannot fingerprint' mean 'unchanged'.

item: Boundary Train: target_label_encoder (LabelEncoder)
detail: Fitted sklearn LabelEncoder, pickle-only, in _NEVER_PERSIST. Set only when the target dtype is object/category/bool; POPPED otherwise. Page 07 re-applies it to raw y (`if label_encoder is not None and y_raw.dtype == object`) — if the encoder is stale relative to the current frame's categories, .transform raises ValueError inside a bare `except Exception: pass`, silently degrading to the X_test fallback path.
ev: pages/06_Train_and_Compare.py:485-491; pages/07_Explainability.py:198-205
act: record the class mapping (JSON: List[str] classes_) in Project; rebuild the encoder in Jobs
note: Accurate at HEAD, and the failure path is worse than the row states because of where the except sits. item: Four of nine repair kinds renumber rows, invalidating row identity mid-analysis
detail: promote_header, drop_empty_rows and drop_rows all end in .reset_index(drop=True); melt_repeated rebuilds the index. The project keys rows by label, so any label stored before such a repair now points at a different row. A sealed lockbox SURVIVES the repair and afterwards names different rows — the seal looks intact and is not. This is a different failure from T0-STRUCT-002: not two components disagreeing on a convention, but one repair invalidating the convention, which no agreement between components prevents. PR #145 removed the same pattern from apply_plausibility_filter; these four are the remainder of the class.
ev: ml/import_doctor.py apply_fix — promote_header / drop_empty_rows / drop_rows / melt_repeated
act: Adopt the identity barrier (ROADMAP Decision A): repairs that change what a row IS run only before the lockbox is sealed; repairs that remove rows preserve survivor labels. Tests: no post-barrier op changes a surviving row's index; pre-barrier repairs unreachable once sealed.
note: The barrier is a phase rule now. The project owns the lockbox, so the project is what refuses: sealing raises the barrier, and promote_header and melt_repeated are unreachable behind it because they rebuild what a row IS — afterwards the sealed labels name different rows and nothing downstream can detect it, since a stale lockbox still looks well-formed. drop_rows and drop_empty_rows stay allowed on both sides: they only remove rows, survivors keep their labels, and preview_fix already reports by content whether a given drop renumbered anything. Both tests the decision asks for are in: no post-barrier operation changes a surviving row's index (a repair is applied after sealing and every sealed label still names the same row, checked by value), and a frame renumbered after the barrier is detected rather than absorbed. Enforced at the API's apply path, not only available as a method. Named regression test on the phase rule itself.
verified_ev: turbotab/project.py check_repair_allowed · PRE_BARRIER_ONLY_FIXES

item: The pre-registered routing baseline was not frozen: the test suite rewrote it on every run, and had done so since the Router landed
detail: tests/integration/test_routing_baseline.py::test_measure_classic_and_commit_the_baseline called measure.write_baseline(BASELINE, ...) on docs/turbotab/data/routing-baseline.json - the artifact VALUE_CHECK_PREREG.md names as the reference every threshold is banked against, and which the prereg says in as many words must not be edited after Router code exists. The protection was temporal and stated only in a docstring: 'It is written now, while the Router does not exist, so it cannot be fitted to.' That was true at 6bfe598 and became false when ml/router.py landed at L8. Nothing announced the expiry, so from L8 onward every make verify re-measured Classic WITH the Router present and committed the new numbers over the reference. The L9 task-3 commit (cebe6f6) shipped one such re-measurement before it was caught and reverted in 7c8339a. The same defect applied to routing-baseline-leaky.json.
ev: tests/integration/test_routing_baseline.py:299 (write_baseline on the frozen path) and :342 (the leaky one); docs/turbotab/VALUE_CHECK_PREREG.md:5 names the artifact and the commit; commits cebe6f6 (drift shipped) and 7c8339a (reverted)
act: Split measurement from comparison: the suite compares, an explicit script measures and refuses to overwrite a frozen baseline. Stamp the artifact with measured_at and assert it against the commit the prereg names. Record the expiring-guarantee rule in FEATURE_PARITY.md beside the principle-locality corollary, and audit every 'before X exists' guarantee whenever X ships.
note: Fixed at L9, and the damage was contained: the frozen file's measurements are byte-identical to 6bfe598 (verified field by field), so no re-measurement ever landed on the reference except the one in cebe6f6, which was reverted the same day. Only a schema-additive change reached it before that - c8c5f51 added pull_affordances and mode without moving a number - and that is the only kind of change this artifact may take. THE FIX, in three parts. (1) The harness stops writing: test_measure_classic_and_commit_the_baseline is now test_classic_still_measures_what_the_baseline_recorded, which re-measures in memory and compares, with a failure message that says in words 'Do not fix this by re-measuring. Record the new measurement beside the old one and adjudicate.' Writing moved to scripts/remeasure_routing_baseline.py, which the suite never calls, requires an explicit --out, refuses any protected path, refuses to overwrite an existing file, and prints what moved. (2) Provenance: both baselines carry measured_at and prereg as top-level keys, and the named test asserts measured_at equals the commit parsed out of the prereg, then reads that commit out of git and asserts every metric the prereg's table quotes is unchanged - a self-declared stamp proves nothing on its own, so the swap-proof half is the values check. (3) The rule is recorded, not just the instance: FEATURE_PARITY.md gains the expiring-guarantee corollary beside principle-locality, because both are silence rather than failure - one fails across space, this one across time. The drift this exposed (denominator 9 -> 10 on messy-clinic, 1 -> 2 on longitudinal) is adjudicated in VALUE_CHECK_ADJUDICATION.md with both denominators reported; the frozen file is unmodified and the new measurement sits beside it as routing-baseline-l9.json. L18: THE NAMED GUARD WAS REPOINTED, because the L18 skipped-guard check found it does not run here. test_the_frozen_baseline_is_the_one_the_prereg_names calls pytest.skip mid-test when git cannot read 6bfe598 — this clone is shallow — and A MID-TEST SKIP ERASES THE ASSERTIONS THAT ALREADY PASSED FROM THE REPORT: the stamp assertion above the skip runs and passes, and pytest still reports the node as SKIPPED. So the row rested on a guard that reads as running nothing. It now names test_the_adjudicated_reference_differs_from_the_frozen_one_only_as_ruled, which runs here and is the stronger guard anyway: it compares the frozen baseline against the adjudicated one metric by metric and fails on any difference the adjudication did not rule, so a rewritten baseline is caught by VALUE rather than by provenance stamp. Revert-probed at L18: moving questions_asked from 34 to 35 in the frozen file turns it red with 'moved beyond what was ruled'. The git-read provenance test is kept and still runs wherever history is complete.

item: physiology_reference.match_variable_key matches by substring, so any column whose name contains a reference key is measured against that variable's intervals
detail: match_variable_key returns the first reference key that is a substring of the lowercased column name. On the L9 drive fixture, hba1c_proxy matched hba1c and 75 of 160 rows were reported outside the impossibility band - not because the values were impossible but because the column is not HbA1c. The same collision is available for glucose_flag, weight_change, bp_sys_delta, height_percentile and any derived column that keeps its parent's name. The consequence is worse than a wrong label now that the impossibility band exists: the improbable tier is advisory, but the impossible tier PROPOSES DELETING ENTRIES, so a naming coincidence can propose deleting real data.
ev: ml/physiology_reference.py match_variable_key (`if key in col_lower`); ml/card_evidence.py plausibility_report calls it per numeric column; ml/dataset_profile.py:616 does the same for the advisory tier
act: engine - match on the column name as a token sequence rather than as a substring, and require the match to be the whole name or a name segment. Until then the >25% guard is the containment, not the fix.
note: Fixed on the adjudicator's ruling: exact key or declared alias, nothing else. The L9b containment - a closed list of modifier words - was a denylist answering an allowlist question, and the ruling names exactly why it could not work: hba1c_proxy was caught because _proxy was listed, and hba1c_v2, hba1c_imputed and hba1c_lab2 were not. Three of those four inherited HbA1c's floor and its licence to propose deleting entries. match_variable_key now normalizes case and separators and compares for EQUALITY against the variable key and its declared aliases; an unrecognized name gets no bounds and no flags, which is the governing rule's may-be-silent branch taken deliberately. Saying nothing about hba1c_lab2 is a gap; applying HbA1c's floor to it is the app asserting something it does not know. Aliases are how a real column earns its bounds: declared per variable in the reference, readable, and covering the spellings that actually occur (a1c, hemoglobin_a1c, dbp, diastolic, serum_glucose, and the NHANES column codes LBXGH, BPXDI1, LBXGLU and friends). Three tests hold it: eight unrecognized names yield silence from match_variable_key AND produce no block from plausibility_report; nine exact keys and aliases still earn their bounds, so silence has not become the answer to everything; and every declared alias is unique to one variable, because two variables claiming one alias would make the match order-dependent. STILL OPEN, and now filed as its own row: ml/clinical_units.infer_unit has the identical substring match and it decides the conversion factor that is actually APPLIED in the preprocessing pipeline. See T0-BUILD-004. The plausibility path is safe because match_variable_key gates it first, but the harmonization path is not gated by anything. sibling-of: the theory_anchors substring fallback named in FEATURE_PARITY.md - the pedagogy registry pair STILL has no key-match test, and it fails in the safer direction (drops a link) where these two add a wrong claim.
verified_ev: ml/physiology_reference.py match_variable_key (exact key or declared alias); DEFAULT_NHANES_REFERENCE aliases per variable

item: clinical_units.infer_unit matches by substring and decides the conversion factor actually applied to the data
detail: infer_unit picks a clinical variable with `if var_name in col_lower`, the same substring match T0-BUILD-003 removed from physiology_reference. Measured: infer_unit('weight_change', ...) returns unit='kg', conversion_factor=1.0 at HIGH confidence; infer_unit('glucose_flag', ...) returns unit='mg/dL'; infer_unit('hba1c_proxy', ...) returns unit='%'. This is worse than the reference match because of where it lands: ml/pipeline.py:60 build_unit_harmonization_config calls it per numeric column and appends the factor to the positional list handed to UnitHarmonizer, which MULTIPLIES the column by it inside the fitted pipeline. A derived column whose values happen to fall in a different-unit hypothesis range therefore gets silently rescaled - a lb-to-kg factor of 0.453592 applied to a weight_change that is already in kg, with no error and no flag. The plausibility path is not exposed: card_evidence gates on match_variable_key first, which is now exact. The harmonization path is gated by nothing.

The distinction from the physiology_reference version is the one the adjudicator drew: that one flagged values falsely, this one CONVERTED them, because ml/pipeline.py:60 feeds the factor into the positional list UnitHarmonizer multiplies by inside the fitted pipeline. weight_change matched weight and came back kg at high confidence, so a column of kilogram differences was eligible to be rescaled by 0.453592 the moment its values sat in the pounds range - a wrong number, no error, in the data that gets modeled. Thirteen resembling names now earn nothing (weight_change, weight_delta, weight_pct, hba1c_v2, hba1c_imputed, hba1c_lab2, hba1c_proxy, glucose_flag, glucose_missing, bmi_zscore, bp_sys_delta, height_percentile, waist_ratio) - the set a closed modifier list could never have covered. Silence has not become the answer to everything: fifteen exact keys and aliases still match, and a genuine weight column in pounds still earns its 0.453592. The test that proves the fix at the site that applies it calls build_unit_harmonization_config and asserts weight_change gets factor 1.0. THE TWO REGISTRIES ARE NOW PINNED TOGETHER. CLINICAL_VARIABLES and DEFAULT_NHANES_REFERENCE name the same eleven variables and now publish the same aliases, with test_the_two_name_registries_agree asserting both the key sets and the alias sets match. Drift between them would mean a column earning physiologic bounds but no unit conversion, or the reverse - the plausibility check comparing raw values against converted bounds. FOURTH SUBSTRING REGISTRY, STILL OPEN: utils/theory_anchors.py resolves its 19 keys by substring with a fallback that silently drops a theory link when a finding string is reworded, and the registry pair theory_anchors/theory_demos STILL HAS NO KEY-MATCH TEST - named in FEATURE_PARITY.md 'Two specific things to watch' as the most fragile intelligent feature in the app. It fails in the safer direction (drops a link rather than adding a wrong claim), which is why it is last of the four and not first.

item: The outcome was asked a feature's question - 'is this binary?' - instead of the only one that matters for a target: which level is the event
detail: ml/binary_text.py, built at L9 for GUIDED-001, made no distinction between a feature and the target. On two of the three pre-registered fixtures it fired on the outcome column itself and proposed 'read as binary', which is the wrong question in kind. For a feature, binary-versus-numeric is a READING: the values mean the same thing either way and the question is how to store them. For the outcome the reading is nearly forced - two-level text is binary classification - and the decision that matters is which level is the EVENT being predicted. That choice sets the sign of every effect estimate, decides what sensitivity and specificity are the sensitivity and specificity OF, and determines what the model is trained to detect. Asking 'is this binary?' about an outcome answers a question nobody had and skips the one that does.
ev: ml/binary_text.py positive_class_finding / apply_positive_class; turbotab/engine.py diagnose(target=...) and _dispatch_fix; turbotab/api.py apply and preview carry the choice
act: Route the target to its own question. Never pre-select the event at any confidence; offer convention as a suggestion with its reasoning shown.
note: Raised by the adjudicator from the L9b report, where it was recorded as an observation rather than a row - which was the wrong disposition and is corrected here. Fixed as ruled. detect_binary_text takes the target and routes that column to positive_class_finding, titled 'Which of these is the event you are predicting?' and never the word binary; every other column keeps the feature question. Before a target is chosen there is no outcome column, so every column is read as a feature, which is right. NEVER PRE-SELECTED, AT ANY CONFIDENCE: confidence is pinned at medium so auto_suggestable is False regardless of vocabulary, and a parametrized test covers the conventional case (responder), a known boolean pair (yes/no), the case with no correct default (alive/dead) and one with no convention at all (arm_a/arm_b). Convention is offered with its reasoning shown - responder, improved, case and friends - and alive/dead is deliberately absent from that table with a test asserting it stays absent, because whether the event is death or survival is the research question rather than a property of the data. Applying refuses without a named level and honors a choice that contradicts the suggestion. The API returns the two levels and the suggestion instead of a preview when no event is named, because previewing 'set the event' with no event would have to pick one. DENOMINATOR CONSEQUENCE, adjudicated: the inventory swapped repair::binary_text__outcome for repair::positive_class__outcome on two datasets. Composition changed, no metric moved, every threshold still passes - see VALUE_CHECK_ADJUDICATION.md 'The denominator moved again'.
verified_ev: ml/binary_text.py positive_class_finding / apply_positive_class; turbotab/engine.py diagnose(target=...) and _dispatch_fix; turbotab/api.py apply and preview carry the choice

item: Classic decides which class is the event by alphabetical order, silently and with no way to see or change it
detail: ml/splits.py:300 encodes a categorical target with LabelEncoder().fit_transform(y.astype(str)). LabelEncoder sorts classes, so class 1 - the event, the positive class, the one every metric is about - is whichever level sorts LAST alphabetically. Measured on the project's own fixtures: messy-clinic gets responder over non-responder, which happens to match convention; the longitudinal fixture gets 'stable' over 'improved', so the model is trained to detect NOT improving; alive/dead would make death the event. Everything downstream inherits it - the sign of every coefficient, which class precision and recall describe, which way a calibration curve bends, what an odds ratio is an odds ratio OF - and nothing in the Classic interface states the choice or offers to change it. The numbers are internally consistent and answer a question the analyst may not have asked.

Note the interaction with T0-BUILD-004 and the label-encoder: neither is a crash, both are silent wrong-direction answers, and both are invisible in a results table that looks entirely reasonable. detail: tests/test_shap_and_sensitivity.py::TestSHAPComputation has three tests that import shap. That is a DELIBERATE and documented exclusion: requirements-dev.txt says shap pulls numba/llvmlite and is slow to build, and calls the three failures 'a small and legible gap rather than a misleading one'. The half that is neither deliberate nor documented is the other side. The root requirements.txt DOES pin shap>=0.42.0 and .github/workflows CI installs it, so CI would run these three - but the workflow triggers only on push to main and pull_request to main, and this work is on TurboTab under hard rules that forbid pushing to main and opening a PR. So the tests do not run locally by design and do not run in CI by branch, and the intersection is: they have not executed at all for L9, L9b and L9c. TestPermutationImportance and TestSensitivityAnalysis in the same file DO run; the uncovered surface is SHAP value computation specifically - the LinearExplainer and TreeExplainer paths and the assertion that SHAP feature names line up with SHAP values.

act: Decide the gap rather than inherit it. Either (a) run the SHAP tests in an environment that has shap before pages/07 is extracted, or (b) mark them skipif-shap-absent so the suite reports a SKIP rather than a FAIL and the gap is legible in the output instead of in a requirements comment. Do NOT solve it by installing shap into turbotab/.venv: it pulls numba/llvmlite into a pinned pandas<3 envelope and would trade a legible gap for a dependency risk.
note: Filed at L9c on the adjudicator's ruling that an untested subsystem must stop reading as background noise. Reported at the end of L9, L9b and L9c as 'the same three pre-existing failures, unrelated' - true each time, and cumulatively it means the SHAP path has been unverified across three loops of engine changes. Nothing in those loops touched SHAP, which is why the failures stayed identical; that is reassurance about the past and no guarantee about the next change. IT MATTERS NOW because pages/07's SHAP orchestration is on the extraction list, and extraction without characterization is exactly what TRANSITION_PLAN warns against - the same argument SWEEP-015 makes about models/. Whichever option is taken should land before that extraction starts. The skipif option is the cheaper one and closes only the legibility half: a SKIP says 'not run here' where a FAIL says 'broken', and the current output says the wrong one of those three times per loop.

item: Sentinel detection manufactured the gap that condemned real answers: a 1-9 Likert scale had its 9s recoded to missing
detail: Finding 26. The check excluded 7/8/9 as candidate sentinels BEFORE measuring the spread. item: A list-valued JSON field is silently converted to its Python repr and becomes a text column
detail: A record like {'SEQN': 1, 'visits': [1,2,3]} loads with a 'visits' column holding the string '[1, 2, 3]'. Nothing says the value was stringified. item: The same subject lands in both training and the sealed test set whenever detect_repeated_subjects' ratio gate misses - silently, with a clean lockbox chip
detail: From docs/audit/HUNT_FINDINGS.md lockbox-subject-leak-heuristic-gates, verified at HEAD. detect_repeated_subjects has two independent gates, each sufficient on its own to defeat the quarantine. GATE 1, utils/test_lockbox.py:218-219: rows_per = n / k; if rows_per < 1.5 or rows_per > 50: continue. Partial repeated measures - only some subjects have a second visit, the commonest real cohort shape - falls under 1.5. A many-to-many merge product falls over 50. GATE 2, the whole-token name list _SUBJECT_ID_TOKENS: a column the list does not name is not considered at all. Both paths return None, ensure_lockbox has no other source of a group column, and the chip renders the ordinary non-grouped text that mentions neither subjects nor a fallback.
ev: REPRODUCED AT HEAD (1e2701d), three of the audit's four shapes: (a) 100 subjects with 30 second visits, rows/subject 1.30 -> detect_repeated_subjects None, group_col None, 7 of 100 subjects on both sides. (b) 10 subjects x 60 rows after a many-to-many merge, rows/subject 60 -> None, None, 10 of 10 on both sides. (c) key named 'SUBJ', 60 subjects x 3 visits -> None, None, 23 of 60 on both sides. CONTROL: the same shape keyed 'SEQN' returns ('SEQN', 60, 180) and leaks 0 of 60. utils/test_lockbox.py:218-219 (ratio gate), :100-110 (_SUBJECT_ID_TOKENS)
act: engine - the ratio gate is the load-bearing half and has no defensible floor: 1.30 rows per subject IS repeated measures, and 60 is a merge artifact that repeats harder, not less. Remove the bounds or replace them with a test of whether ANY value repeats. Failing that, the chip must not claim a lockbox: the app may be silent and may refuse, but a seal that does not seal is the one thing it may not assert.
note: The same subject lands in both training and the sealed test set whenever detect_repeated_subjects' name/ratio heuristic misses. GUIDED DOOR: BUILT AND TESTED. L13 shipped the grain question in turbotab/grain.py, AnalysisProject.set_grain and engine.draw_holdout: the question is asked before the seal, seal_lockbox REFUSES while grain is None (so clause 01's ordering is a precondition rather than a comment), the heuristic supplies only the suggestion, and the seal records seal_basis plus basis_source. Measured on this row's own fixture - 60 subjects x 3 visits keyed SUBJ - the Guided seal is basis 'grouped', source 'user_stated', and 0 subjects appear on both sides where the Classic path puts 23 of 60. CLASSIC: UNCHANGED, so this row is OPEN and not FIXED. resolved-in-core; closes at L11 convergence of pages/01_Upload_and_Audit.py. utils/test_lockbox.ensure_lockbox still infers, and tests/test_the_seal_states_its_basis.py::test_KNOWN_GAP_an_unrecognized_id_name_is_still_recorded_as_cross_sectional still PASSES - verified by running it - because it pins Classic's path, not Guided's. item: find_key_candidates draws an independent 5,000-row sample per file, so value overlap is measured between unrelated row subsets — the true key is dropped entirely above ~50k rows and mis-quoted 4x-150x too low below that

act: See the original entry; dispositioned against HEAD at L11.
note: Closed at L12 against measured revert-failure, not topical proximity. tests/test_key_sampling_is_symmetric.py already existed but did NOT cover this defect: a revert probe restoring independent per-side sampling in _key_tokens - in both its recorded forms, positional head-truncation and an N-row .sample(random_state=42) per side - left all seven of its tests green. Because the wrapper loop returns first, that refusal is unreachable whenever any one of the seven wrapper names is present - which is most API exports. The choice between candidate row sets is then made by the position of a name in a hard-coded tuple, not by anything about the file.
ev: data_processor.py:124 (_JSON_WRAPPER_KEYS), data_processor.py:284-287 (the wrapper loop), data_processor.py:290-292 (the single-list-key path it also pre-empts), data_processor.py:302-307 (the refusal that can no longer fire)

That is FALSE for the upload path users actually take, and the correction matters more than the original claim. data_processor.inspect_json at :406-419 collects EVERY top-level key holding a non-empty list as a candidate, uses the wrapper list only to pick a DEFAULT, and returns a note reading 'Several keys hold lists (data, records). Reading rows from data - change it below if that is wrong.' pages/01_Upload_and_Audit.py:406-424 renders that as a selectbox plus a caption. So on pages/01 the user is told and can correct it, and JsonLayout's own docstring says this was built precisely because 'this app does not guess silently'. What actually remains, and why the row stays OPEN at reduced severity: (1) the refusal text at :302-307 is genuinely unreachable dead code, since the wrapper loop returns first - harmless but misleading to a reader, who will believe the loader refuses ambiguity when it does not; (2) load_tabular_data itself still resolves ambiguity by a name's position in a tuple, so every caller that does not front it with inspect_json gets the silent behavior. detail: L12 lens 6 (JSON structure), fresh adversarial pass. data_processor.py:295-296 returns pd.DataFrame(obj) whenever every value of a top-level object is itself a dict. pd.DataFrame over a dict-of-dicts uses orient='columns' semantics, so the OUTER keys become columns. For the two shapes that actually reach this branch - a payload keyed by participant ID, and pandas' own to_json(orient='index') - the outer keys are ROW identities, so the table arrives with its axes swapped. The branch cannot tell orient='columns' from orient='index' because both are dicts of dicts, and it assumes one without saying so.

Where a marker exists use it; where it does not, ask which way round the table is, showing both readings with their row and column counts. Never pick silently. A cheap contradiction check helps the default: if the inner dicts all share a small key set and the outer keys are many, the outer keys are almost certainly rows.

A pandas round-trip reproduces it exactly: a (3,2) frame indexed P1..P3 exported with to_json(orient='index') reloads as (2,3) with columns P1,P2,P3. NOT CAUGHT DOWNSTREAM: the Import Doctor's only remark on the 3x500 frame is wide_repeated_measures at info severity and low confidence, so nothing in the app disputes the shape. SEAL-CLASS: yes by consequence - a transposed frame has no row identity that corresponds to a participant, so grain, detect_repeated_subjects and the seal are all computed over variables-as-rows.

item: A single blank ID in a JSON file collapses every participant ID above 2^53 into one value at LOAD time - the exact false merge join_doctor defends against, created before join_doctor can see it
detail: L12 lens 7 (JSON encoding), fresh adversarial pass. json.loads parses integers with arbitrary precision, so large IDs survive parsing intact and pd.json_normalize gives an int64 column. But a single null in that field makes the column float64, and float64 cannot represent consecutive integers above 2^53. Two distinct participants therefore become one ID before any join, any grain question or any seal. ml/join_doctor.py:_canon_scalar carries a docstring saying exactly this - 'passing IDs through float64 silently collides values above 2^53 ... which is a false merge - the worst outcome this module can produce' - and canonicalizes with arbitrary-precision arithmetic to prevent it. That defense is bypassed here because the collapse happens in the loader, upstream of everything join_doctor inspects.
ev: data_processor.py:_json_obj_to_frame:246 (pd.json_normalize over the record list); contrast ml/join_doctor.py:_canon_scalar, whose docstring names this as the worst outcome it can produce
act: Detect the shape at load: an integer-valued field carrying nulls, whose non-null magnitudes exceed 2**53, must not be materialized as float64. Read it as a nullable Int64 or as text and say so. The check is cheap and the failure is unrecoverable downstream, which is the argument for spending a gate here. Compare the float64-id-collapse HUNT entry (its slug is spelled the British way in docs/audit/, which is the exempt path precisely so a quoted record stays quotable), which is the same collapse reached through the join path - the two share a root cause and neither closes the other.
note: REPRODUCED AT HEAD through the real loader. [{SEQN: 9007199254740993, glucose: 95}, {SEQN: 9007199254740992, glucose: 102}, {SEQN: null, glucose: 110}] loads with SEQN dtype float64, and the two IDs compare EQUAL - nunique on the non-null values is 1 where there are 2 real participants. CONTROL, which is what makes the trigger precise: the identical file with the null row removed loads as int64 with 2 distinct values [9007199254740993, 9007199254740992]. One blank ID is the entire difference. SEAL-CLASS: YES. Two participants sharing an ID is corrupted row identity at its root - the grain question, detect_repeated_subjects, group_col and the seal all read a table in which two people are one person, and the seal will happily place 'them' on one side of the split while the data holds two.
verified_ev: data_processor.py:_json_obj_to_frame:246 (pd.json_normalize over the record list); contrast ml/join_doctor.py:_canon_scalar, whose docstring names this as the worst outcome it can produce

item: latin-1 sits ahead of cp1252 in the JSON encoding fallback and never raises, so cp1252 is unreachable and Windows exports load with control characters where their punctuation was
detail: L12 lens 7 (JSON encoding), fresh adversarial pass. data_processor.py:144 and :158 both try ['utf-8','utf-8-sig','utf-16','latin-1','cp1252'] in order and return the first that does not raise. latin-1 is a total 1:1 byte-to-codepoint mapping - it decodes all 256 byte values and cannot fail - so it is a catch-all, and the cp1252 entry positioned after it can never be reached. The two codecs differ exactly on the 0x80-0x9F range, which is where cp1252 puts smart quotes, en and em dashes, ellipsis and the euro sign; latin-1 maps that range to C1 control characters. Excel and Windows tooling emit cp1252 routinely.
ev: data_processor.py:144 (_json_read_text path branch), data_processor.py:158 (buffer branch) - the same list in both, with cp1252 after latin-1
act: Two changes, both small. Order cp1252 before latin-1, since cp1252 is a strict superset of the useful part of latin-1 for text that came from Windows. And keep latin-1 as the last resort it is, but disclose when it was used - a decode that cannot fail is not evidence the encoding was right, so silently succeeding is the wrong report. Better still, sniff for a BOM and for the 0x80-0x9F range before choosing.
note: REPRODUCED AT HEAD. A record whose note field reads "fasting's baseline - 90-95 mg/dL" with cp1252 smart punctuation (0x92 apostrophe, 0x97 em dash, 0x96 en dash) is written as cp1252 and loads back as 'fasting\x92s baseline \x97 90\x9695 mg/dL' - C1 control characters in place of the punctuation, with no warning. The correctly decoded string differs. Verified separately that latin-1 decodes bytes(range(256)) without raising, which is what makes cp1252 dead code. SEAL-CLASS: no. Filed high rather than critical because the damage is confined to text content and does not change row identity or counts - but a corrupted categorical level is a distinct level, so category variants and any name-based matching see values no human typed.
verified_ev: data_processor.py:144 (_json_read_text path branch), data_processor.py:158 (buffer branch) - the same list in both, with cp1252 after latin-1

item: Duplicate keys in a JSON record collapse silently with the last value winning, so a repeated field discards the earlier value with no count and no warning
detail: L12 lens 7 (JSON encoding), fresh adversarial pass. The JSON specification permits an object to carry the same key more than once and does not say which wins; Python's json.loads resolves it by keeping the LAST occurrence. Nothing in the load path uses object_pairs_hook to detect the collision, so a record carrying a field twice - which happens when exports are concatenated or a schema changes mid-file - silently loses one of the values, and the frame that results is well-formed.
ev: data_processor.py:176 (_json_lines_to_records) and the json.loads calls in the load path - none passes object_pairs_hook
act: Pass an object_pairs_hook that counts repeated keys and surfaces them, then either refuse or load with an explicit note naming the fields and the number of records affected. This is a disclosure fix rather than a semantics fix - there is no correct choice between the two values, which is precisely why the app must not make one silently.
note: REPRODUCED AT HEAD. The record {"SEQN": 1, "glucose": 95, "SEQN": 2} loads as SEQN 2, glucose 95 - the first SEQN is gone. Through the real loader a two-record file yields SEQN [2, 3] where the file's first record names both 1 and 2. SEAL-CLASS: borderline, and worth watching rather than claiming. When the duplicated key is the identifier, as in the reproduction, the row's identity is chosen arbitrarily by document order, which puts it in the same family as IMPORT-209; when it is an ordinary measurement it is data loss and nothing more. Filed high on the ordinary reading and cross-referenced to 209 for the identifier reading.
verified_ev: data_processor.py:176 (_json_lines_to_records) and the json.loads calls in the load path - none passes object_pairs_hook

item: The JSON loader accepts the non-standard NaN, Infinity and -Infinity literals, so an infinity enters the working table as an ordinary value
detail: L12 lens 7 (JSON encoding), fresh adversarial pass. Python's json.loads accepts NaN, Infinity and -Infinity by default even though RFC 8259 has no such literals, and the load path does not pass parse_constant to reject or flag them. A file carrying Infinity therefore produces a float column holding inf, which propagates through any aggregate computed over it.
ev: data_processor.py:176 and the other json.loads call sites - none passes parse_constant
act: Pass parse_constant to convert NaN to a missing value explicitly and to refuse the infinities with a message naming the field, or to record them as an Import Doctor finding at critical severity the way impossible values are handled. Note the constitution's impossibility pass is the natural home for this: an infinite measurement is the clearest possible impossible value.
note: REPRODUCED AT HEAD. [{bmi: 22.1}, {bmi: Infinity}, {bmi: 27.3}] loads as [22.1, inf, 27.3] with mean inf and max inf. Filed medium rather than high because an infinite mean is conspicuously broken rather than plausibly wrong - it is closer to the app being visibly silly than to it asserting something false, and a researcher will notice. The NaN literal is the quieter half: it becomes an ordinary missing value with no record that the file said NaN rather than null. SEAL-CLASS: no.
verified_ev: data_processor.py:176 and the other json.loads call sites - none passes parse_constant

item: check_header_in_later_row computes a graded confidence score, compares it to a threshold and then throws it away, reporting every detection as high - the one tier the UI pre-selects, and the tier that suppresses all other findings
detail: L12 lens 9 (Import Doctor), fresh adversarial pass. ml/import_doctor.py:315-330 scores each candidate row as uniqueness x stringiness x fill-rate and keeps the best, then :331 rejects anything below 0.5. Everything that clears that bar is emitted at :344 with a hardcoded confidence='high' and severity='critical'. ShapeFinding.auto_suggestable at :99-101 is exactly `confidence == 'high'`, so every header detection is pre-selectable. And diagnose() at :861-863 returns ONLY the header finding when one is present, by design, because a misplaced header makes every other symptom derived. Those three facts compose: a detection at the threshold and a certain one are indistinguishable, both are pre-selected, and both silence the rest of the review.
ev: ml/import_doctor.py:315-331 (the score and its threshold), :344 (confidence hardcoded 'high'), :99-101 (auto_suggestable is confidence == 'high'), :861-863 (the masking short-circuit in diagnose)
act: Map the score onto the confidence tiers instead of discarding it - comfortably above the bar is high, near it is medium or low - and make the masking short-circuit conditional on the tier. A header finding the app is unsure of should be reported ALONGSIDE the other findings, not instead of them. That is the governing rule applied to the check's own uncertainty: high means the app is asserting, and a score of exactly 0.50 is not an assertion. This also disarms IMPORT-132 without needing to retune either threshold, which matters because both thresholds are defensible and it is their combination on narrow frames that fails.
note: REPRODUCED AT HEAD, both ends of the range measured. The IMPORT-132 narrow-frame false positive scores 0.500 and reports high / critical / auto_suggestable True. A genuine three-column NHANES title block scores 1.000 and reports high / critical / auto_suggestable True. Identical output for a marginal guess and a certain reading. SEAL-CLASS: no directly, but note the compounding - promote_header is one of the repair kinds T0-ID-001 identifies as renumbering rows and therefore invalidating row identity, so a pre-selected false positive at score 0.50 rebuilds what a row IS. This is the root cause behind IMPORT-132 rather than a duplicate of it: 132 is the specific narrow-frame trigger, 216 is why the trigger is so expensive when it fires.
verified_ev: ml/import_doctor.py:315-331 (the score and its threshold), :344 (confidence hardcoded 'high'), :99-101 (auto_suggestable is confidence == 'high'), :861-863 (the masking short-circuit in diagnose)

item: Clause 01 contradiction: the impossibility pass runs AFTER the seal in Classic, and its row-dropping form silently shrinks the sealed test set
detail: L12 clause-01 sequence check, file-don't-fix. The constitution fixes the pre-seal order as load, structural repairs and the impossibility pass, grain, eligibility, SEAL, EDA - and gives the reason: a split computed over corrupted values is a worse split, and impossible entries are normally an exclusion that changes N and belongs in the flow diagram before anything is sealed. Classic runs it in the opposite order. The seal is drawn at pages/01_Upload_and_Audit.py:1106 the moment the target is chosen, with the comment 'Quarantine the test set NOW, before any target-aware analysis can see it'. The impossibility pass is the physiologic plausibility check, and it lives at pages/02_EDA.py:1758 - one page later, post-seal. Its row-dropping form is later still: pages/05_Preprocess.py:894 calls apply_plausibility_filter over the WHOLE frame and writes the result to session_state['filtered_data'], which utils/session_state.py:196-212 then serves to every page as the working table.
ev: pages/01_Upload_and_Audit.py:1094-1106 (the seal, drawn at target selection); pages/02_EDA.py:1758 (the plausibility check, one page later); pages/05_Preprocess.py:890-897 (apply_plausibility_filter over the whole frame into filtered_data); utils/session_state.py:196-212 (get_data serves filtered_data as the working table); ml/pipeline.py:109-132
act: Move the impossibility pass to page 01, before ensure_lockbox is called - it is row-local and label-free, so by clause 06 it is a structural repair that may execute immediately, and clause 01 puts it pre-seal for the split-quality and flow-diagram reasons rather than for leakage reasons. Until it moves, the post-seal filter must not be able to remove sealed rows silently: either refuse and route the user back to a re-seal, which clause 04 says is its own hard logged decision, or disclose the shrink at the point it happens.
note: PARTIAL at L13, and the split is deliberate. WHAT LANDED: the measured harm is gone. Clause 04 says a robustness trim applies to the training partition only and that trimming the test set to match is permanently off the menu; the page-05 plausibility filter ran over the whole frame into filtered_data, which get_data() serves to every page, so it silently removed sealed rows - measured at 7 of 60, evaluation on 53. Sealed rows are now put back whole and the page says so, routing a user who genuinely wants the narrower population back to the pre-seal question. Revert probe: deleting the restore turns test_the_page_still_restores_them red, and the unrestored trim demonstrably does remove sealed rows (asserted as the guard's own premise, so it cannot pass vacuously). WHAT DID NOT LAND, AND WHY I STOPPED RATHER THAN HALF-DOING IT: the sequence itself. Clause 01 puts the impossibility pass before the seal; it still runs at pages/02_EDA.py:1758, one page after. Moving it means BUILDING A PLAUSIBILITY SURFACE ON pages/01, which has none at all - verified by grep, not assumed. That is new construction on a frozen path, and the freeze is lifted for repair. Worth stating precisely, because it changes what the residual is worth: of clause 01's two stated reasons, the exclusion-changes-N one is the filter, and it is now fixed; the worse-split one barely bites in Classic's actual split logic, which stratifies on the TARGET and groups on an ID - impossible values in features do not move either. The residual is the participant-flow argument, which is real and belongs with the step that owns eligibility. NOT FILED AS A REGISTER ROW, and the reason matters: the register's states are both / classic-only / core / guided-only, all of which answer 'which door has this'. NEITHER door has it, so any state I picked would be a false claim about one of them - I tried 'neither' and register.py check rejected it, correctly. The convergence phrase therefore lives here instead: resolved-in-core; closes at L11 convergence of pages/01_Upload_and_Audit.py. A register row becomes right the moment one door builds it. NOW COVERS BOTH DOORS: Guided has a seal as of L13 and its impossibility pass is also post-seal, so this row is no longer Classic-only. TRACKS CLAUSE `lockbox-01`, obligation the-impossibility-pass-comes-before-the-seal. Named explicitly at L16: the rebuilt coverage matcher requires a row that tracks a clause to say WHICH clause, because nothing otherwise distinguishes it from a row about a similar-sounding thing.
verified_ev: pages/05_Preprocess.py (the trim now restores sealed rows and says so); ml/pipeline.py apply_plausibility_filter; pages/02_EDA.py:1758 (the impossibility pass, still post-seal); pages/01_Upload_and_Audit.py:1106 (the seal, still first)

item: HUNT casefold-decided-per-column: normalize_key decides case-folding from the column it is normalizing, so one stray-case value on one side puts the two files in different canonical spaces
detail: normalize_key computes fold_case per call as 'folding does not reduce the number of distinct IDs', and each side of a join is normalized by a SEPARATE call - diagnose_join, repair_keys and execute_join each normalize left and right independently. A single case collision anywhere in one column disables folding for that column only, so the left side compares as 'a01' while the right compares as 'A01'.
ev: ml/join_doctor.py normalize_key (fold_case computed from `text.str.lower().nunique() == text.nunique()` on the single column passed in); the independent per-side calls in diagnose_join, repair_keys and execute_join
act: Decide folding ONCE for the pair and pass it explicitly to both calls - normalize_key already takes fold_case as an override, so the machinery exists and only the decision site is wrong. The safe joint rule is to fold only when folding is non-destructive on BOTH sides, and to say so when it is not.
note: REPRODUCES AT HEAD, exactly as recorded. sites.specimen = ['A01','B02'] normalizes to ['a01','b02'] (folded, no collision). labs.specimen = ['A01','a01','B02'] normalizes to ['A01','a01','B02'] (NOT folded, because folding would merge A01 and a01). diagnose_join then reports matched_keys=1 and predicted_rows=1, and execute_join returns 1 row - the recorded 'Result: 1 rows' for a pair that shares two specimens. The asymmetry is visible directly in the two normalize_key outputs. SEAL-CLASS: yes by consequence - the surviving row is a mis-pairing, so identity is wrong before anything downstream runs. Note the same entry appears twice in HUNT as asymmetric-case-folding-misjoins-ids; one defect, two filings, dispositioned here once.
verified_ev: ml/join_doctor.py normalize_key (fold_case computed from `text.str.lower().nunique() == text.nunique()` on the single column passed in); the independent per-side calls in diagnose_join, repair_keys and execute_join

item: HUNT float64-id-collapse-* (the full slug in docs/audit/ spells it the British way, which is why it is abbreviated here): IDs above 2^53 arriving already stored as float64 are collapsed, and the resulting duplicates are explained to the researcher as repeated visits

item: HUNT decoy-key-passes-index-guard: the index-like penalty requires BOTH sides to be row counters, so a measurement column paired against a counter escapes it entirely and outranks the honest pairing
detail: index_like is computed as _looks_like_row_index(left) AND _looks_like_row_index(right), and both the confidence downgrade and the score penalty key off that conjunction. A small-integer measurement (age, visit number, parity, dose) paired against a row counter therefore has index_like False, escapes the penalty, scores above the genuinely index-like pair, and becomes suggest_best.
ev: ml/join_doctor.py:599 (index_like as the conjunction of both sides), :293-299 (the confidence branch that keys off it), and the score penalty that does likewise
act: Penalize the pair when EITHER side is a bare counter, not only when both are. A counter on one side is enough to make the overlap meaningless, because a 1..N counter overlaps anything 1..N by construction. The conjunction is the wrong Boolean.
note: REPRODUCES AT HEAD, exactly as recorded and with the ranking inverted as described. Two unrelated 50-row files, each carrying a 'row' counter plus one measurement: find_key_candidates returns ('age','row') at MEDIUM with index_like=False and score 0.312, ahead of ('row','row') at LOW with index_like=True and score 0.150. suggest_best returns ('age','row','medium'). The honest pairing is correctly penalized and the nonsense one is not, so the penalty makes the ranking worse than no penalty would. SEAL-CLASS: YES by inheritance - a medium-confidence junk key fuses two unrelated cohorts, and combine_ui offers medium in the dropdown with the top-scoring candidate pre-selected (see IMPORT-203). Same family as the HUNT entry index-like-key-accepted-silently, which is the both-sides-counter case and is dispositioned separately.
verified_ev: ml/join_doctor.py:599 (index_like as the conjunction of both sides), :293-299 (the confidence branch that keys off it), and the score penalty that does likewise

item: HUNT stack-source-column-clobbered: re-stacking a table this app exported rewrote every provenance label and delivered one column fewer than promised
detail: execute_stack assigned SOURCE_COLUMN unconditionally, clobbering any existing column of that name, and StackPlan.summary() computed the width as len(all_columns) + 1 with no check for SOURCE_COLUMN already being present - so the promise and the delivery disagreed by one column while the user's own provenance labels were silently replaced.

Two exports each carrying their own __source_file with values orig_1999 / orig_2001 stack to columns ['SEQN','__source_file_before','age','__source_file']: the user's column is preserved under __source_file_before with its labels intact, and the app's own column carries exportA / exportB. summary() promises 'Result: 4 rows and 4 columns ... plus one column recording which file each row came from' and delivers exactly 4 - the off-by-one is gone. That is a disclosure gap rather than a data defect, and preserving the data under a legible name is defensible, so it does not justify a row of its own; it is noted here so a future reader does not mistake the silence for the old clobbering. item: HUNT stack-conflicts-only-checked-on-shared-columns: the dtype-conflict check iterates only the INTERSECTION of column sets, so a column that drifts in and out across cycles is mixed into one object column with no warning at all
detail: plan_stack compares dtype families only across plan.shared_columns - the intersection of every file's columns. A column present in some cycles and absent from others is therefore never compared, however incompatibly its types differ where it IS present. The recorded fix is to iterate the union and compare across the files that actually have the column.

Three cycles where LBXIN is float in 1999-2000, text in 2001-2002, and absent from 2003-2004: plan.shared_columns is ['SEQN'] alone, plan.blocking and plan.warnings are both EMPTY, and execute_stack produces an LBXIN column of dtype object holding [3.1, 4.2, '3.1', '4.2', nan, nan] - floats and strings side by side. item: HUNT stack-no-duplicate-subject-or-row-detection: overlapping subjects and exact duplicate rows are stacked with zero warning, inflating n and putting the same person on both sides of the seal
detail: plan_stack builds its whole diagnosis from column names and dtypes; total_rows is a plain sum and is the only row-level statement it makes. There is no candidate-ID scan, even though ml/join_doctor.py already has the machinery - normalize_key and value-overlap measurement - to do one.

act: Scan for a candidate ID column across the stacked files and report the overlap before the stack, in the same voice the join path uses for fan-out. The stack path is the only assembly route with no value-level check at all, and it is the one that changes n.
note: REPRODUCES AT HEAD, exactly as recorded. Two cycles of 50 subjects sharing 25 of them stack to 100 rows with plan.blocking, plan.warnings and plan.notes ALL EMPTY; the result holds 75 distinct SEQN with 25 duplicated. The app promises 100 rows and delivers 100 rows, so the row-count promise is honest - what is missing is that 25 of those people are counted twice. SEAL-CLASS: YES, and this is the sharpest one in the batch. A duplicated subject in a stacked table is the exact condition the lockbox exists to prevent: unless grouping is detected, the same person lands in training and in the sealed test set, and held-out performance reads better than it is. Constitution 02 makes this the grain question, and nothing on the stack path asks it.
verified_ev: utils/combine.py plan_stack (diagnosis from names and dtypes only; total_rows as a sum); the reusable machinery at ml/join_doctor.py normalize_key / find_key_candidates

item: HUNT stack-hint-steers-cycles-to-link: the relationship hint reads schema drift as evidence of different measurements, so eight NHANES cycles are confidently steered to the join screen
detail: relationship_hint decides purely from len(shared) / len(union) against fixed thresholds. Cycles of one survey share a demographic core and drift in their lab panels, which pushes that ratio into the 'link' band - the opposite of the truth. combine_ui then maps the hint to a default radio index, and 'unclear' is not neutral either: it also resolves to the join screen.
ev: utils/combine.py relationship_hint (the shared/union ratio and its thresholds); utils/combine_ui.py:457 default_idx, where both 'link' and an unrecognized hint map to index 0
act: A ratio over column NAMES cannot distinguish stacking from linking, because the distinguishing evidence is in the VALUES - stacked cycles have disjoint IDs, linked files have overlapping ones. Measure that instead, and make the unknown case genuinely neutral rather than silently the join screen. This is the same demotion constitution 02 applies to grouping heuristics: offer a suggestion, detect contradictions, do not decide.
note: REPRODUCES AT HEAD. Eight cycles sharing SEQN, RIDAGEYR, RIAGENDR and RIDRETH1 with lab panels drifting in and out give shared 4 of union 17 = 0.24, and relationship_hint returns 'link'. These are the same measurements on different people - the textbook stack - and the app pre-selects the join screen, where the same SEQN across cycles would produce a fan-out rather than a stack. Confirmed separately that combine_ui's default_idx maps 'link' to 0. SEAL-CLASS: no directly, but it routes the user into the operation that multiplies rows, and IMPORT-241 is what happens if they take the correct route instead.
verified_ev: utils/combine.py relationship_hint (the shared/union ratio and its thresholds); utils/combine_ui.py:457 default_idx, where both 'link' and an unrecognized hint map to index 0

item: HUNT stack-int-float-id-precision: an integer subject-ID column stacked with a float one is silently widened to float, and above 2^53 that merges two participants into one
detail: _dtype_family returns 'number' for both int64 and float64, so a cycle whose IDs are integers and one whose IDs are floats - which happens as soon as a single ID is blank - raise no conflict, and pd.concat widens the column to float64. act: Treat integer and float as distinct families for a column that looks like an identifier, or - better and cheaper - refuse to widen any integer column whose magnitudes exceed 2**53 and say why. Same repair as IMPORT-209 and IMPORT-234, which are this defect on the JSON load path and the join path: three routes, one rule, and it should be written once.
note: REPRODUCES AT HEAD, AND IS WORSE THAN FILED - this is why the severity is raised from the recorded 'minor' to landmine. Ordinary case: int64 SEQN [1,2,3] stacked with float64 [4.0,5.0,nan] gives a float64 column [1.0,...,5.0,nan] with plan.warnings and plan.notes both EMPTY. Large-ID case, which the entry did not test: SEQN [9007199254740993, 9007199254740992] stacked with a float column comes back float64 holding [9007199254740992.0, 9007199254740992.0] - the two participants are no longer distinguishable, and `values[0] != values[1]` is False. No warning at any point. SEAL-CLASS: YES. Two participants sharing an ID is corrupted row identity, and this is the third independent route to the same collapse in this loop: IMPORT-209 at the JSON loader, IMPORT-234 at the join, IMPORT-260 at the stack. That convergence is the finding worth carrying forward - the guard belongs at one chokepoint, not three.

item: Lockbox constitution clause 05 - the extrapolation obligation - is implemented nowhere and tested nowhere: a train-only trim arms a requirement that never fires
detail: L14, found by tests/test_every_clause_is_tracked.py on its first run, and it is the clearest justification for writing that check. Clause 05 says a train-only trim is a LEGITIMATE choice, so it earns no blocker - friction is spent where an operation is almost certainly an error and this one is not. What is illegitimate is reporting a single aggregate metric afterwards as though nothing happened. So the trim silently ARMS a requirement, and the blocker fires AT EXPORT if the stratified in-range / out-of-range breakdown is absent. Neither half exists: nothing records that a trim was applied in a way that arms anything, and nothing at export checks for the breakdown.
ev: grep for 'extrapolat' across tests/, turbotab/, ml/ and utils/ returns ZERO hits at L14. Contrast pages/05_Preprocess.py, which performs exactly the trim clause 05 is about (the plausibility filter in 'filter' mode), and ml/pipeline.py apply_plausibility_filter
act: Two pieces, and the ordering matters because the second is useless without the first. (1) When a train-only trim is applied, record it on the project as an armed requirement - the trim itself stays frictionless, which is the clause's whole point. (2) At export, refuse a single aggregate metric while that requirement is armed and the in-range / out-of-range breakdown is absent. Note this is the same shape as the acknowledgment machinery the routing constitution already has for blockers, so the mechanism exists and the wiring does not.
note: SPLIT AT L16 on the product owner's instruction, and the ARMING HALF IS NOW FIXED. This row is the arming half only; STATE-105 carries the FIRING half at export, which has nowhere to live until the Report step exists. TRACKS CLAUSE `lockbox-05`, obligation a-train-only-trim-arms-the-obligation. WHY THE SPLIT MATTERS, in the product owner's own reasoning: a clause whose obligation fires at a different step from the action arming it is the one most likely to go unbuilt, and under a SINGLE row, landing the arming half would have read as progress on the whole clause. Under two, this one closes and the other stays visibly open. WHAT SHIPPED: turbotab/obligations.py records what a decision obliges a LATER step to say, and project.trim_training_rows narrows the training partition and arms it. The trim earns no blocker - clause 05 says it is a legitimate choice and friction is spent where an operation is almost certainly an error. THE NUMBER THE REPORT CANNOT RECOVER is computed at trim time and this is the crux: the held-out rows were never trimmed because clause 04 forbids it, so some of them lie OUTSIDE the range the model was fitted on, and a single aggregate metric averages them in silently. After the trim the out-of-range training rows are gone, so the report cannot count what is no longer there - which is why an obligation that only said 'something was trimmed' would be useless. THE TRIM OBEYS CLAUSE 04 AT THE OPERATION: training rows only, sealed rows never touched, verified by a test that also asserts its own premise - that surviving sealed rows include ones outside the range, or the test could not tell 'sealed rows were kept' from 'sealed rows were trimmed too'. A pre-seal trim is refused and the refusal NAMES THE OTHER OBJECT: before the seal, narrowing the study is an eligibility criterion, a different question that changes N. EIGHT REVERTS each red for its own reason, including one that removes both the sealed-row exclusion AND the project's own identity assertion, so the named test is the thing under test rather than the belt-and-braces guard that fires first. AND THE ABSENCE IS ASSERTED: test_the_firing_half_is_deliberately_absent_and_tracked fails if STATE-105 is closed or if this module grows a refuse_export, so 'the firing half is not built' is a statement the suite makes rather than a thing a reader has to notice.
verified_ev: turbotab/obligations.py; turbotab/project.py trim_training_rows; turbotab/test_the_trim_arms_the_obligation.py (8 tests); STATE-105 carries the firing half

NO: structural repair, row-local and label-free, executes immediately on the working table and posts a receipt. item: User-facing copy lives at ~105 raise sites and 51 markup literals, so the copy deck can only be half generated and its hand-assembled half is protected by probes rather than by construction
detail: L15, found while building docs/turbotab/COPY_DECK.md. Generation was attempted first and is only partly possible. The catalogues are data and generate cleanly: features.CATALOGUE (20 strings), selection.METHODS (6), router.plan()'s questions (8), and grain's answers, exits and disclosures (16). The rest are f-strings raised at the point of failure - 48 in api.py, 32 in project.py, 9 in features.py, 7 in selection.py, 9 in router.py - plus 51 string literals inside web/index.html's markup. Extracting those would need either an AST walk that cannot resolve the interpolations or a runtime harness driving every error path, and both produce a WORSE artifact than transcribing them, because a half-resolved f-string is not reviewable copy.
ev: docs/turbotab/tools/copydeck.py (the split, and the measurement table in its docstring); the 30 HAND entries there, each naming its source file
act: Move user-facing strings out of their raise sites into a catalogue the way features.CATALOGUE already does it - the pattern exists in this codebase and works. Then copydeck.py generates the whole deck and the probe mechanism becomes unnecessary. Do NOT do this by adding a translation layer: the goal is that copy is DATA, which is what makes it reviewable, and an i18n indirection that still scatters the strings solves nothing.
note: FILED RATHER THAN WORKED AROUND, which was the instruction and is also the right call: the difficulty is a fact about where copy lives, and a deck assembled quietly by hand would have hidden it. WHAT PROTECTS THE HAND HALF MEANWHILE, stated as weaker rather than sold as equivalent: each hand entry carries a probe - a distinctive fragment of the real string - and copydeck.py check asserts that fragment is still in the file it came from, matching on a whitespace-and-quote-squashed form so rewrapping does not count as drift. That catches a string that CHANGED. It does not catch one that was ADDED, which is the real gap and the reason this row stays open. The check is in the pre-commit hook. IT EARNED ITSELF IMMEDIATELY: on first run it caught 15 of my own 30 transcriptions as wrong - 8 because the probe spanned an implicit line-continuation and 7 because I had transcribed the sentence from memory rather than from the file. A hand deck drifts from the moment it is written, not later.

item: The archive's whitelist has silently dropped project state twice - the seal's basis at L13 and the entire features record at L14 - and both were caught only because a test happened to be written for that feature
detail: L16 ruling. turbotab/archive.py build_members is an explicit whitelist and should be: a serializer that walks whatever it finds writes whatever it finds, and 'never persist participant data' would then depend on nobody adding the wrong field. But a whitelist has exactly one failure mode and this one has hit it twice. L13: the seal gained seal_basis and basis_source per constitution 03, lockbox.json did not, so a restored seal came back unable to say what it rested on - the group_col None ambiguity 03 exists to remove. L14: the project gained engineered, deferred_transforms, selection_spec and features_settled, config.json did not, so a restored project had the engineered COLUMNS from the parquet and no record of how they got there, and the deferred specs were gone outright with nothing else holding them.
ev: tests/test_the_archive_carries_every_field.py; the two prior regressions are pinned by name inside it as well as by the general check
act: Closed.
note: FIXED at L16, structurally rather than a third time by hand. TWO LEVELS, because the whitelist has two. Level 1: every dataclass field on AnalysisProject is classified PERSISTED or REGENERATED-with-a-reason, a field in neither fails, and every persisted field is populated with a NON-DEFAULT value before the round trip - asserted, not assumed, because a fixture that left a field at its default would pass on an archive that never wrote it. Level 2: every KEY of the nested dicts that carry their own whitelists, the lockbox and the cohort. Level 1 cannot see inside those - lockbox is ONE field and it survives level 1 while losing half its keys, which is L13 exactly. PARAMETRIZED per field so a failure names what was lost: 'the archive lost selection_spec' rather than 'the archive lost something'. ONE THING THE TEST HAD TO LEARN: the lockbox member MATERIALIZES DEFAULTS - a seal with no strata comes back with strata [] - so the restored dict is a superset and strict equality would fail on an archive that lost nothing. The field-level claim for those two is arrival; the key-level claim is preservation. REVERT PROBE, six reverts each red for its own named reason: dropping engineered from config.json, dropping seal_basis from lockbox.json, dropping deferred_transforms, dropping the READER half for selection_spec (written but not read back is the same loss), dropping one cohort key, and adding a new unclassified field to the project - the last is the case the file exists for and it fails with 'a field whose persistence nobody decided'.
verified_ev: tests/test_the_archive_carries_every_field.py; the two prior regressions are pinned by name inside it as well as by the general check

item: Lockbox constitution clause 07 - missingness routes by dtype AND mechanism - is implemented nowhere, and the first coverage matcher passed it on a wildcard that matched a file of unrelated helper tests
detail: L16, found by the rebuilt matcher. The old manifest linked clause 07 to ('tests/test_missingness_encoding.py', 'test_') - a WILDCARD fragment, so the clause was covered by the file existing. That file tests has_data_indicator, identify_features_with_missing and conditional_ordinal: encoding utilities. It asserts nothing about clause 07's actual obligations. Those are: ask FIRST whether missingness is informative and default to an explicit Missing category or indicator; treat imputing an informatively-missing field as a BLOCKER with typed acknowledgment; record the STABILITY ASSUMPTION - that missingness means the same thing at deployment - as a methods assumption, because it may not hold across sites; fit numeric imputation INSIDE the fold; and never place the outcome in the imputation model, which is a blocker in any configuration.
ev: tests/test_every_clause_is_tracked.py, the `lockbox-07` obligations; tests/test_missingness_encoding.py, whose ten tests are all about encoding helpers
act: Build at the Preprocess step, which is the next loop's subject. Two obligations are listed separately in the manifest because they fail differently: the categorical branch fails by imputing away a signal, the numeric branch by leaking the outcome into the imputation model.
note: FIXED at L17. The wildcard link is gone: `lockbox-07`'s two obligations now name tests that assert the clause rather than a file of encoding helpers. WHAT SHIPPED, and the ORDER is the substance. The MECHANISM question is asked PER COLUMN and BEFORE the strategy - 'Could a blank in X mean something?' - because the answer decides which strategies are legitimate at all; asked the other way round, a column that carried information gets a median written over it by a well-meaning default. It is a FACT that is never skippable, for the same reason as the grain: the app cannot know. 'I'm not sure' is first-class and deliberately does NOT block, because turning an admission of uncertainty into a wall teaches people to stop admitting it. THE TWO BRANCHES FAIL DIFFERENTLY and are separate objects. Categorical: an explicit Missing category and an indicator are ROW-LOCAL by clause 06's litmus and execute now; imputing a column the user has called informative is a CONSEQUENCE with a TYPED acknowledgment and both terminal exits attached, since they may know something the app does not. Numeric: the outcome inside a MICE scope is REFUSED outright and no acknowledgment gets round it - clause 07 says it is a blocker in any configuration, so it is not offered as a choice. THE STABILITY ASSUMPTION is recorded on the declaration when a mechanism is stated informative, as an ASSUMPTION rather than a warning: a warning is dismissed, an assumption is carried by a manuscript. THE RECEIPT is the step's hard design problem - almost every preprocessing transform is stateful, so a user answers several questions and the table does not move. plan_receipt reports the counts honestly, leads with the deferred count rather than the zero, and says WHY nothing changed, ending on what the user actually accomplished: 'the part that cannot be automated'. TEN REVERTS each red for its own named reason, including inferring the mechanism, dropping the attest exit, letting the outcome into MICE, executing a stateful strategy on the working table, and the indicator filling the value it was supposed to leave blank. FOUR OF THE TEN WERE MY OWN BAD REVERTS OR WEAK ASSERTIONS FIRST TIME, caught by the harness's red-for-the-wrong-reason verdict - which is the L16 rule paying for itself twice in one loop.

item: The 'ask only when the choice changes the answer' check was wired so that it could never fire on any dataset

note: Found while counting suppressions for the L18 report, which is the only reason it was found at all. As first built, the endpoint short-circuited on may_be_preselected BEFORE consulting the divergence check, and the only operation with a divergence function (scale) is model-determined - so every row that could be measured was skipped before measuring, and every row that was measured had nothing to measure against. n_choices_suppressed was structurally zero and would have stayed zero forever. This is the silence family in a new place: a check that nothing triggers is a check that does not exist, and it reads as 'the mechanism found nothing to suppress' rather than 'the mechanism never ran'. FIXED by separating the two axes. Determinacy decides whether the row is a question at all; divergence decides whether a pre-selected fact's VARIANT is worth raising. Whether a model gets scaled inputs is the model's property and the table settles it; which scaling, once it happens, is a judgment about this data. Operations now name their PUSHED alternatives - measure.py's own push-the-notable-pull-the-rest applied to variants - and a variant with no pushed alternative returns (False, None), an absence rather than a suppression, so the count cannot include questions that never existed. Measured after: 5 of 5 suppressed on a Gaussian fixture, 0 of 5 on a heavy-tailed one, same code path. ALSO GREEN, because the restated copy was character-identical, and an identity check passes on a duplicate right up until somebody edits one side - which is the drift itself rather than a guard against it. So the test now asserts the DEPENDENCY: the pack's prior is replaced with a sentinel and the rendered sentence has to follow. A restating implementation renders the original and fails, and the third probe is red for 'there are two implementations of the averaging rule again'.
